subject: Information Theory
title: Entropy in Passwords
description: A fast breakdown of Entropy in Passwords for builders.

hook.text: 'password123' has low entropy. A hacker's dictionary cracks it in seconds. A random 20-character string? Years.

buildup.text: Password entropy measures how hard it is to guess. Each bit of entropy doubles the search space.

discovery.text: A random 8-character lowercase password: about 37 bits. Add uppercase, digits, symbols: jumps to about 50 bits.

twist.text: Human-chosen passwords have far less entropy than random ones. Patterns, names, and dates are predictable.

climax.text: Password managers generate high-entropy strings. The human only needs to remember one master password.

punchline.text: More entropy means harder to guess. That simple.

quiz.question: Why do human-chosen passwords have low entropy?
